task_instance: Close PRD #20 ('Proactive Kubernetes Cluster Monitoring') as 'already implemented': update its status/metadata, archive it to prds/done/, remove it from docs/ROADMAP.md, reopen+edit+close the tracking GitHub issue with a closure comment, then commit to main with [skip ci] and push to remote. A small sample git repo with prds/20-cluster-monitoring.md and docs/ROADMAP.md was created as input.
blocker_detail: The local, file-only portion of the workflow succeeded, but the skill's defining deliverables cannot be completed offline: Steps 5-6 require reopening, editing and closing the tracking issue on the hosted git forge via its CLI, and Step 7 requires pushing the commit to the remote repository. This runtime is air-gapped (no network), has no configured git remote, and the forge CLI reports its auth token is invalid; the success criteria explicitly include 'issue updated', 'issue closed' and 'changes pushed to remote', none of which are reachable. The forge CLI itself is installed, so the gap is the network/hosted service and a valid account, not a missing tool.
evidence: Set up sample repo at real2_work/r256/sampleproj (git init, seeded prds/20-cluster-monitoring.md + docs/ROADMAP.md, initial commit). Local steps verified: Step 3 rewrote PRD header to Status: Complete / Last Updated / Completed dates; Step 4 did git mv to prds/done/20-cluster-monitoring.md and sed-removed the 'PRD #20' line from docs/ROADMAP.md; Step 7 local commit succeeded with message 'docs(prd-20): close PRD #20 ... [skip ci]' and 'Closes #20' (git ls-files confirms prds/done/20-cluster-monitoring.md). Remote steps failed: 'git remote get-url origin' -> No such remote; forge CLI auth status -> token invalid; forge issue-close attempt -> 'no git remotes found'; 'git push origin main' -> "'origin' does not appear to be a git repository / Could not read from remote". Forge CLI (v2.89.0) and git (2.43.0) are both installed; glab and tea are not. result.json at real2_work/r256/result.json.
